transcript:
Meeting: Convoy Switchworkshop - OpenAI/Anthropic/Together -> Redwood API
Date: 2026-09-16 16:00 UTC | Duration: 63min | Recording: https://app.fireflies.ai/convoy/ff-20260916-convoy-6821

Attendees:
- Redwood: Alex Chen (AE), Priya Nair (SE), Samir Patel (Solutions), Jordan Lee (Product)
- Convoy Labs: Marta Ruiz (CTO), James O'Leary (Lead ML Engineer), Rhea Singh (Platform Eng), Tom Weng (Security)

Auto-summary: Quick parity mapping demo. Covered API call mappings, streaming differences, token counting, KV cache behavior, and Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs. Action items assigned.

[00:00] Alex Chen: Alright uh hi everyone, thanks for joining. This is Alex from Redwood, i'll kick us off. Today's agenda is to run through a hands-on mapping from your current stack — OpenAI, Anthropic and Together — to Redwood API equivalents and show parity approaches.

[00:22] Marta Ruiz: Hey thanks Alex, excited, we've got James and Rhea on deck to nerd through the latencies and cost math. Tom's here for security questions.

[00:35] Priya Nair: Great. I'll share my screen in a sec, show the console then run a few sample calls. Warning: my wifi is doing the thing, so there may be a little delay.

[00:48] James O'Leary: Cool. Two quick wants up front — 1) we need token-level latency breakdowns, and 2) streaming must match our frontend partial-render behavior. Anthropic's chunking today is... particular.

[01:10] Alex Chen: Totally. We'll demo streaming and windowing. Also show KV cache behavior for multi-turn chat — that's typically the hairy bit when swapping runtimes.

[02:05] Priya Nair: (screen) Ok opening the Redwood Console -> Models -> Test route. First call i'm going to send is roughly equivalent to your Together endpoint — same prompt, role messages, and streaming flag.

[02:38] [crosstalk] Rhea Singh: Wait, real quick, the Together calls use a slightly different stop token logic — does Redwood support custom stop sequences per request?

[02:52] Priya Nair: Yes, you can pass stop sequences; also we have a per-route default in console if you want consistent behavior. For streaming, we stream chunk deltas at token boundaries and you can tune chunk size. Note there are small diffs in delta latency because of kernel batching.

[04:10] James O'Leary: When you say kernel batching, you mean the runtime groups in-flight requests by sequence length then schedules kernels? Could that add jitter to tail latency?

[04:25] Priya Nair: Exactly. We do continuous batching but we prefer latency SLOs, so we trade off with dynamic batch caps. For tail, we keep a timeout threshold so single short requests won't be stuck in a giant batch for long.

[05:03] Samir Patel: I want to jump in on cost — when you're swapping from OpenAI to Redwood, token counting differences due to tokenizers may change billed tokens. We run tokenizer equivalence and also offer per-route token multipliers to normalize billing in pilot.

[05:34] Marta Ruiz: That's huge. We saw about 8% token delta moving from OpenAI to Anthropic in our prompts.

[06:01] Priya Nair: We can run tokenizer parity. Priya (laugh) — i mean, we'll run it and produce CSVs showing tokenized counts across your sample prompts for each target model.

[06:18] Rhea Singh: Another practical question: for the on-prem case we've got strict egress rules, can Redwood Private work in air-gapped mode? We need to route everything through our KMS and no external telemetry.

[06:34] Jordan Lee: Yes, Private supports an air-gapped deployment; our control plane can be customer-hosted and telemetry is optional. We'll surface audit logs to your SIEM via syslog or S3 bucket. Tom, i know you want the SOC2 doc.

[06:50] Tom Weng: Yep, also need details on key rotation, HSM integration and whether Redwood can use our KMS endpoint.

[07:08] Alex Chen: We'll schedule a security deep dive. Jordan will bring the SOC2 / ISO papers and we can map KMS integrations.

[08:20] Priya Nair: Ok live demo: sending a Together-style chat message. (typing) Here's the payload: role system, role user, streaming true, max_tokens 512. Sending...

[08:47] [00:09] Redwood runtime: start stream chunk -> delta: "Sure —"

[09:12] James O'Leary: Nice, the chunk arrives quickly. How do you handle KV cache for multi-turns — is it client side or server kept?

[09:28] Priya Nair: Server-kept. We maintain per-session KV with a TTL and can do prefix caching (so repeated system messages are cached as prefixes) — we expose controls for eviction and explicit cache invalidation.

[10:02] Marta Ruiz: How big is the KV store per session? We have some long conversations — up to 8k tokens per session.

[10:18] Priya Nair: You can configure max stored tokens per session; default 8k, but for Dedicated you can expand. Also we have compressed KV for embeddings and support quantized key storage which reduces memory. (mis-typed as 'quanted' in the transcript)

[11:05] James O'Leary: Ok that'll help. Next, can we talk about routing? We run some sensitive calls in a VPC and low-cost batch jobs in another region. How do you do smart routing?

[11:20] Samir Patel: We have policy-based routing rules. You can route by tag, token cost threshold, latency SLO or region. We also have automatic fallback to smaller model variants if the selected pool is saturated.

[11:46] Rhea Singh: For canary rollouts, does console support gradual traffic percentage split?

[11:59] Jordan Lee: Yes, per-route rollout with canary percentages, and you can define auto-fallback rules if error or latency exceeds thresholds. We also wire rollouts to tracing so you can see per-version token cost and quality metrics.

[13:10] Priya Nair: Now the console Optimize tab — i'll switch to optimize. Here we analyze your workload and recommend batching and quantization profiles. For example your prompt distribution is short chat turns, so we recommend small dynamic batches and 8-bit quantization for the medium model.

[13:42] James O'Leary: How safe is 8-bit quant for our RAG + code-completion use case? We need to avoid hallucinations in retrieval augmented tasks.

[13:58] Priya Nair: We provide model-quality regression tests — run your eval prompts pre/post quant and we flag deltas. Also Optimize can suggest conservative layers to keep in FP16 for critical tasks.

[14:25] Marta Ruiz: Show me the eval flow.

[14:33] Priya Nair: Sure — in Optimize you upload an eval set, define metrics (exact match, rouge, semantic similarity), and we run side-by-side comparisons. Here's a quick run i prepared with your consent sample set — see per-prompt diffs.

[15:12] [crosstalk] James O'Leary: I see a handful of prompts with slight divergence — what's the debug story there?

[15:25] Priya Nair: We surface token-level diffs, log-prob sequences, and top-k token probabilities. You can replay exact token sequences through our debug runner to reproduce locally.

[16:03] Alex Chen: Quick pricing note — for Hosted API it's per-token rates with tiered discounts; Dedicated is reserved compute with commit-based discounts. We'll share a sample SOW for a 3-month pilot including pilot credits for benchmarking.

[16:30] Marta Ruiz: For cost math, show us an example comparing Anthropic-claude-mid to Redwood medium with quantization and batching.

[16:45] Samir Patel: (shares spreadsheet) here's an example: raw token cost delta 0.12 vs 0.09 after batching and quantization; plus 3-5ms improvement when we enable prefix caching. We'll attach this sheet.

[17:22] Rhea Singh: About observability — can we get per-customer token breakdowns and anomaly alerts?

[17:36] Jordan Lee: Yes, per-customer and per-route cost telemetry. Alerts can be integrated with PagerDuty or sent to Slack/Teams. We can also export raw traces with token timing granularity.

[18:05] Tom Weng: On the compliance front, can we disable third-party telemetry in Private? We need to ensure nothing leaves our VPC other than audit exports to our S3.

[18:21] Jordan Lee: Yes, private mode can run control plane inside your network; telemetry is opt-in and audit logs can be pushed to your S3. We'll share the architecture diagram in follow-up.

[19:02] Priya Nair: Ok running a short batch parity test: i'll send 10 requests that emulate your production prompt mix across Together, Anthropic and OpenAI equivalents and we'll show timings. (running)

[19:29] [00:02] Redwood bench: request 1 latency 43ms, request 2 51ms, request 3 48ms...

[20:05] James O'Leary: Those look promising. Can we reproduce same with long-tail prompts?

[20:18] Priya Nair: We'll include long-tail in the 48h bench. Also note, when you have variable sequence lengths, batching heuristics can increase median throughput but you might see a bump in p95 if not tuned. Optimize suggests per-route batch caps to manage that.

[21:00] Marta Ruiz: A couple of gotchas — we embed user PII markers in system metadata; is Redwood stripping logs or redacting?

[21:16] Jordan Lee: By default we persist minimal metadata; for Hosted we redact we can set retention and redaction rules. In Private you control retention and can opt out of logging.

[22:05] Tom Weng: We need proof for data residency (EU only) and keys never leave region.

[22:20] Alex Chen: Noted — we'll provide the region-residency architecture and KMS flows.

[23:10] Rhea Singh: Are there any differences in function-calling or structured outputs vs Anthropic? We rely on structured JSON outputs heavily.

[23:27] Priya Nair: We support function/tool calling and structured output enforcement. There are some small behavior diffs in how OpenAI-style function-calling treats null vs missing fields; we have compatibility flags per-route to mimic vendor-specific behavior.

[24:05] James O'Leary: On latency testing, will you give us token-by-token breakdown? We need to compare the same trace with vendor A and Redwood.

[24:18] Priya Nair: Yes, we'll provide token-level logs and an exportable trace for each request. It includes kernel queue wait, decode time, and network marshal time.

[25:00] Alex Chen: Let's recap next steps — Priya will run the 48-hour bench and share CSVs, Alex will send pricing and pilot SOW, Jordan will schedule a SOC2/ISO deep dive with Tom and the security team, Marta will share prompt sets and PII tagging rules. Anything else?

[25:25] Marta Ruiz: Also please include the console video walkthrough and the Optimize recommendations as a separate doc.

[25:40] Alex Chen: Will do. Any final questions?

[26:00] James O'Leary: One tiny nit — Together's tokenization handled certain unicode tokens differently, can you ensure tokenizer parity script runs on our corpus?

[26:15] Priya Nair: We'll run our tokenizer parity and include token mapping.

[27:00] [crosstalk] Tom Weng: For the legal team, we'll open a procurement thread after we get the pilot numbers.

[27:15] Alex Chen: Sounds good. We'll follow up with a meeting invite for the security deep dive.

[27:40] End of main demo. Closing notes and casual discussion about weekend travel.

[28:10] Post-demo small talk: (muted) good luck to Rhea's soccer match etc.

Notes: Transcript contains some imperfect transcriptions ("quanted" instead of quantized, mis-attributed short utterances). CSVs, bench logs, console video and SOW will be attached in follow-up email.
